title: Finite models and decidability of intuitionistic propositions

based_on.title: Intuitionistic Logic (ILLC report PP-2006-25; ESSLLI 2005 lectures)
based_on.pages: Section 3.3 printed pp. 17–19, Theorem 13 finite-model claim and Exercise 15.

based_on.title: Filtration (March 14, 2012)
based_on.pages: Full one-page note, especially definitions, implication step and canonical theory traces; repair atom valuation outside Sigma and assume subformula closure.

summary: Compress canonical worlds to finite traces, bound countermodels, and decide finite intuitionistic consequence by an exhaustive finite table scan.
abstract: A failed intuitionistic deduction can be witnessed by an ordered model, but completeness alone does not say how large that model must be. For a finite list of premises and a conclusion, only finitely many subformulas need to be remembered. We record which of these formulas belong to each prime theory and order the resulting finite traces by inclusion. The resulting model preserves every tracked formula and gives a computable bound on the number of worlds needed for a counterexample. Enumerating relation tables, persistent atom tables and designated worlds within this bound then decides the original finite consequence. The proof explains why subformulas must be included and why untracked atom values must be specified.
